assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political economics gave formal and empirical foundations for how electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal institutions shape policy and growth. It is a field-defining body of work that links theory, cross-country evidence and policy-relevant institutional design.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clearest joint originators of the constitutional and electoral-rules programme. Besley is central on state capacity, accountability and fiscal policy. The three-person set is natural, though others, such as Acemoglu and Robinson on institutions, are adjacent and may be credited elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 30 years and is widely taught and cited. Core empirical findings have been tested repeatedly, and the programme is fully mature.
uncertainties: Some causal claims from cross-country constitutional comparisons rest on contested identification.
Overlap with institutions-and-growth work could complicate how credit is split.
Prior committee involvement of one candidate could shape how the case is received.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The political economy of trade policy, including the protection-for-sale framework, and the endogenous-growth-and-trade synthesis changed how economists explain protection and trade's dynamic effects. The work is rigorous, general and influential well beyond trade.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are clearly the joint originators of the central models, so the two-person attribution is clean.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the late 1980s through the 1990s and has had decades of empirical and theoretical follow-up. It is very mature, and a Nobel recognition in trade is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Empirical support for the protection-for-sale predictions is mixed.
Trade has been recognised relatively recently, in 2008, so the committee may weigh field balance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints amplifying and propagating shocks (Kiyotaki–Moore) and the financial accelerator are the standard conceptual basis for credit-cycle macroeconomics and macro-financial policy analysis. The relevance was reinforced by the 2008 crisis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the originators of the credit-cycle mechanism. Gertler is central to the financial-accelerator and macro-finance line with Bernanke, and Bernanke's 2022 prize partly covered related ground. Attribution is somewhat entangled with that prior recognition.
assessment.maturity: Foundational papers date from the 1990s, and the framework is embedded in central-bank and academic models. It is very mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize for banks and financial crises reduces the marginal case.
Whether Gertler or a different co-author is the right third name is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility, neighborhood effects and the long-run effects of place and policy. It combines methodological innovation with large policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader of the programme. Hendren is central on neighborhood and place effects. Katz is credited for the Moving to Opportunity work and earlier labour economics. Friedman is a major co-author, so the three-name limit forces a choice.
assessment.maturity: The work is mostly from the 2010s onward. It is influential and widely replicated in direction, but the long-run policy consequences are still unfolding.
uncertainties: The work is comparatively recent, and the committee may prefer more time.
A large team means credit allocation is contestable.
The weight on measurement versus identified causal mechanisms is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence reshaped understanding of labour demand, polarization, wage inequality and the local costs of trade. The work has broad scholarly and policy influence, including on questions of technology and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure on tasks and the China shock. Hanson and Dorn are the main co-authors on the trade-shock papers. Katz, a coauthor on the earlier skill-biased change work, is a possible alternative, and the task framework also draws on Acemoglu and Restrepo.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from 2003 to 2016. Substantial replication and debate have followed, and the results are well established in broad outline.
uncertainties: Magnitudes of the China shock and the generality of the task framework remain debated.
Credit overlaps with the tasks literature of other scholars.
The work is largely empirical, so the committee may weigh conceptual contribution against measurement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income and wealth series built from tax data changed the empirical basis of inequality research and public debate. The data-construction contribution is major, with substantial influence on public economics.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top-income series, and Zucman extended the work to wealth and offshore holdings. The contributions are distinct but closely tied. Atkinson, now deceased, was an important precursor.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work is over 20 years old and widely used. The wealth and offshore estimates are more recent and more contested.
uncertainties: The wealth-tax and capital-share interpretations are contested, so the committee may separate measurement from theory.
Methodological critiques of the distributional accounts may weaken the case.
Mixing Saez with other candidates' sets could split votes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, with its policy-rule analysis, is the workhorse for monetary policy in central banks worldwide. Its practical and intellectual influence is very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is widely dispersed, among Calvo on pricing, Taylor on rules, Woodford and Gali on the canonical framework, and Christiano, Eichenbaum and others on estimated medium-scale models. The three-name limit makes any selection arbitrary and risks omitting essential contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been developed for around 30 years and is fully established, though the financial crisis and the 2021–23 inflation tested it.
uncertainties: The attribution problem is severe given the many contributors.
The framework's performance in recent inflation episodes and in heterogeneous-agent settings is debated.
Overlap with earlier prizes on macro and monetary policy is possible.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework showed how distortions across firms can account for a large share of cross-country income differences. It connected micro-level data to aggregate development accounting and influenced work on growth and development.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are central through their joint work on misallocation in China and India. Restuccia and Rogerson are closely related, and Restuccia is on the list. The two-name proposal reflects a judgment about the most direct originators, and others' claims are comparable.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from 1997 to 2009. It is well replicated in broad terms, though the magnitudes are contested.
uncertainties: Results are sensitive to measurement error, adjustment costs and the treatment of markups.
Priority is shared with Restuccia and Rogerson and others, so credit is hard to pin down.
Whether the contribution is broad enough compared with larger fields on the list is unclear.
